word_for_word: यद्यप्येवं त्वं सुलभोऽसि ततः किमत आह -- मामिति।
Although in this way You are easy to attain, what follows from that? He says: ‘Having attained Me.’
उक्तलक्षणा महात्मानो मद्भक्ता मां प्राप्य पुनर्दुःखाश्रयमनित्यं च जन्म न प्राप्नुवन्ति।
The great-souled devotees of Mine described above, having attained Me, do not again obtain birth, which is the abode of suffering and impermanent.
यतस्ते परमां सम्यक्सिद्धिं मोक्षमेव प्राप्ताः
For they have attained the supreme and complete perfection, namely liberation.
पुनर्जन्म दुःखानां चालयं स्थानं ते मामुपेत्य न प्राप्नुवन्तीति वा।
Or: having reached Me, they do not obtain rebirth, the abode and seat of sufferings.
एतदेव सर्वेष्वपि लोकेषु पुनरावृर्त्तिं दर्शयन्निर्धारयति -- आब्रह्मेति।
Establishing this very point by showing return in all the worlds, He says: ‘Up to Brahmā’s world.’
ब्रह्मणो भुवनं वासस्थानं ब्रह्मलोकस्तमभिव्याप्य सर्वे लोकाः पुनरावर्तनशीलाः
The world that is the dwelling-place of Brahmā is Brahma-loka; extending up through that, all worlds are subject to return.
ब्रह्मलोकस्यापि विनाशित्वात्तत्प्राप्तानामनुत्पन्नज्ञानानामवश्यंभावि पुनर्जन्म।
Because even Brahma-loka is perishable, rebirth is inevitable for those who reach it in whom knowledge has not arisen.
य एवं क्रममुक्तिफलाभिरुपासनाभिर्ब्रह्मलोकं प्राप्तास्तेषामेव तत्रोत्पन्नज्ञानानां ब्रह्मणा सह मोक्षो नान्येषाम्।
Only those who have reached Brahma-loka through meditations whose fruit is gradual liberation and whose knowledge arises there are liberated together with Brahmā, not others.
तथाचब्रह्मणा सह ते सर्वे संप्राप्ते प्रतिसंचरे। परस्यान्ते कृतात्मानः प्रविशन्ति परं पदम्।
Accordingly it is said: ‘Together with Brahmā, all of them, when the dissolution arrives, at the end of the Highest one’s term, having perfected themselves, enter the supreme state.’
परस्यान्ते ब्रह्मणः परमायुषोऽन्ते कृतात्मानो ब्रह्मभावापादितमनोवृत्तयः
‘At the end of the Highest’ means at the end of Brahmā’s full lifespan; ‘having perfected themselves’ means those whose mental mode has been brought to the state of Brahman.
कर्मद्वारेण येषां ब्रह्मलोकप्राप्तिस्तेषां न मोक्ष इति परिनिष्ठितिः।
The settled conclusion is that those whose attainment of Brahma-loka is through karma do not attain liberation.
मामुपेत्य वर्तमानानां तु पुनर्जन्म नास्त्येवेत्यर्थः।
But for those who abide having attained Me, there is certainly no rebirth; this is the meaning.
ननु च ... इत्यादिपुराणवाक्यैस्त्रिलोक्याः सकाशान्महर्लोकादीनामुत्कृष्टत्वं गम्यते।

But from Purāṇic statements such as ‘Ascetics, charitable men, the dispassionate and forbearing obtain a sorrowless station above the three worlds,’ the superiority of Maharloka and the higher worlds over the three worlds is understood.
विनाशित्वे च सर्वेषामवैशिष्ट्ये कथमसौ विशेषः स्यादित्याशङ्क्य
If all are alike in being perishable, how could that superiority exist? Anticipating this objection,
बहुकल्पकालावस्थायित्वनिमित्तोऽसौ विशेष इत्याशयेन
with the intention that this distinction is due to their enduring for many kalpas,
स्वमानेन शतवर्षायुषो ब्रह्मणोऽहन्यहनि त्रिलोक्या उत्पत्तिर्निशिनिशि च लयो भवतीति दर्शयिष्यन् ब्रह्मणोऽहोरात्रयोः प्रमाणमाह -- सहस्रेति।

and intending to show that in each day of Brahmā, whose lifespan is one hundred years by his own reckoning, the three worlds arise, and in each night they dissolve, He states the measure of Brahmā’s day and night: ‘A thousand yugas.’
सहस्रं युगानि पर्यन्तोऽवसानं यस्य तद्ब्रह्मणो यदहस्तद्ये विदुः
Those who know that day of Brahmā whose limit and end is a thousand yugas,
युगसहस्रमन्तो यस्यास्तां रात्रिं च योगबलेन ये विदुस्त एव सर्वज्ञजना अहोरात्रविदः।
and who by the power of yoga know the night whose end is likewise a thousand yugas—those omniscient persons alone know day and night.
येषां तु केवलं चन्द्रार्कगत्यैव ज्ञानं ते तथाहोरात्रविदो न भवन्ति अल्पदर्शित्वात्।
Those whose knowledge is only through the motions of the moon and sun are not knowers of day and night in that sense, because their vision is limited.
युगशब्देनात्र चतुर्युगमभिप्रेतम्
Here by ‘yuga’ the cycle of four yugas is intended.
चतुर्युगसहस्रं तु ब्रह्मणो दिनमुच्यते इति विष्णुपुराणोक्तेः।
For the Viṣṇu Purāṇa says: ‘A thousand cycles of four yugas are called a day of Brahmā.’
ब्रह्मण इति च महर्लोकादिवासिनामप्युपलक्षणार्थम्।
And ‘of Brahmā’ also indicates the inhabitants of Maharloka and the higher worlds.
तत्रायं कालगणनाप्रकारः।
Here is the method of calculating that time.
मनुष्याणां यद्वर्षं तद्देवानामहोरात्रं।
One human year is a day and night of the gods.
तादृशैरहोरात्रैः पक्षमासादिकल्पनया द्वादशभिर्वर्षसहस्रैश्चतुर्युगं भवति।
By days and nights of that kind, reckoning fortnights and months and so forth, twelve thousand divine years make one cycle of four yugas.
चतुर्युगसहस्रं च ब्रह्मणो दिनम्। तावत्परिमाणैव रात्रिः।
A thousand such four-yuga cycles are Brahmā’s day, and his night is of equal measure.
तादृशैश्चाहोरात्रैः पक्षमासादिक्रमेण वर्षशतं ब्रह्मणः परमायुरिति।
And by such days and nights, reckoned into fortnights, months and so on, one hundred years are Brahmā’s full lifespan.
ततः किमत आह -- अव्यक्तादिति।
What then follows from this? He says: ‘From the unmanifest.’
कार्यस्याव्यक्तं रूपं कारणात्मकं तस्मादव्यक्तात्कारणरूपाद्व्यज्यन्तेऽभिव्यज्यन्त इति व्यक्तयश्चराचराणि भूतानि प्रादुर्भवन्ति।
The unmanifest form of an effect is its causal state; from that unmanifest causal state, the manifestations—the moving and unmoving beings—become manifest and arise.
कदा। अहरागमे ब्रह्मणो दिनस्योपक्रमे।
When? At the coming of the day, at the beginning of Brahmā’s day.
तथा रात्रेरागमे ब्रह्मशयने तस्मिन्नेवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके कारणरूपे प्रलयं यान्ति।
Likewise, at the coming of night, when Brahmā sleeps, they dissolve into that very causal state called the unmanifest.
यद्वा तेऽहोरात्रविद इत्येतन्न विधीयते किंतु ते प्रसिद्धा अहोरात्रविदो जना
Or, ‘those knowers of day and night’ is not an injunction; rather, it refers to those well-known persons who know the day and night.
यद्ब्रह्मणोऽहविंदुस्तस्याह्न आगमे अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः प्रभवन्ति यां च रात्रिं विदुस्तस्या रात्रेरागमे प्रलीयन्त इति द्वयोरन्वयः।
The construction of both statements is: at the coming of the day of Brahmā that they know, manifestations arise from the unmanifest; and at the coming of the night that they know, they dissolve.
तत्र च कृतनाशाकृताभ्यागमशङ्कां वारयन् वैराग्यार्थं सृष्टिप्रलयप्रवाहस्याविच्छेदं दर्शयति -- भूतेति।

There, warding off the doubt that what has been done is destroyed and what has not been done comes to one, and showing for the sake of dispassion the unbroken flow of creation and dissolution, He says: ‘This multitude of beings.’
भूतानां चराचरप्राणिनां ग्रामः समूहो यः प्रागासीत्स एवायमहरागमे भूत्वा रात्रेरागमे प्रलीयते।
The multitude, the aggregate of moving and unmoving living beings, that existed before is this very same one; arising at the coming of day, it dissolves at the coming of night.
प्रलीय पुनरप्यहरागमेऽवशः कर्मादिपरतन्त्रः प्रभवति। नान्य इत्यर्थः।
Having dissolved, it arises again at the coming of day, helpless and dependent on karma and the rest. It is not some other aggregate; this is the meaning.
लोकानामनित्यत्वं प्रपञ्चय परमेश्वरस्वरूपस्य नित्यत्वं प्रपञ्चयति -- पर इति द्वाभ्याम्।
Having elaborated the impermanence of the worlds, He elaborates the eternality of the Supreme Lord’s nature in two verses beginning ‘But higher.’
तस्माच्चराचरकारणभूतादव्यक्तात्परः तस्यापि कारणभूतो योऽन्यस्तद्विलक्षणोऽव्यक्तश्चक्षुराद्यगोचरो भावः सनातनोऽनादिः

Higher than that unmanifest which is the cause of moving and unmoving beings is another, distinct from it, itself the cause of that, unmanifest and beyond the reach of the eyes and other senses, an eternal beginningless reality.
स तु सर्वेषु कार्यकारणलक्षणेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्स्वपि न विनश्यति।
That reality does not perish even when all beings characterized as effects and causes perish.
अविनाशे प्रमाणं दर्शयन्नाह -- अव्यक्त इति।
Showing scriptural authority for its imperishability, He says: ‘The unmanifest.’
यो भावः अव्यक्तोऽतीन्द्रियोऽक्षरः प्रवेशनाशशून्य इति
That reality is unmanifest, beyond the senses, and imperishable, free from entry into change and destruction.
तथाऽक्षरात्संभवतीह विश्वम् इत्यादिश्रुतिष्वक्षर इत्युक्तः
Thus in scriptures such as ‘From the imperishable this universe arises,’ it is called ‘imperishable.’
तं परमां गतिं गम्यं पुरुषार्थमाहुः
They call that the supreme destination, the goal that is the highest human end.
पुरुषान्न परं किंचित्सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः इत्यादिश्रुतयः।
So say scriptures such as: ‘There is nothing higher than the Person; that is the limit, that is the supreme goal.’
परमगतित्वमेवाह -- यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्त इति।
He states its being the supreme goal by saying: ‘Having reached which they do not return.’
तच्च ममैव धाम स्वरूपम्।
And that is My own abode, My very nature.
ममैवेत्युपचारे षष्ठी राहोः शिर इतिवत्।
The genitive in ‘My own’ is figurative, as in ‘the head of Rāhu.’
अतोऽहमेव परमा गतिरित्यर्थः।
Therefore I Myself am the supreme goal; this is the meaning.
तत्प्राप्तौ च भक्तिरन्तरङ्गोपाय इत्युक्तमेवाह -- पुरुष इति।
He states again what was said, that devotion is the intimate means to attaining Him: ‘That Person.’
स चाहं परः पुरुषोऽनन्यया न विद्यते अन्यः शरणत्वेन यस्यास्तया एकान्तभक्त्यैव लभ्यो नान्यथा।
I, that Supreme Person, am attained only by exclusive devotion that has no other refuge, and not otherwise.
परत्वमेवाह।
He states His supremacy.
यस्य कारणभूतस्यान्तर्मध्ये भूतानि स्थितानि।
Within Him, who is their cause, all beings are situated.
येन च कारणभूतेन सर्वमिदं जगत्ततं व्याप्तम्।
And by Him, as the cause, this whole universe is pervaded.
तदेवं परमेश्वरोपासकाः तत्पदं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते अन्ये त्वावर्तन्त इत्युक्तम्।
Thus it was said that worshippers of the Supreme Lord, attaining His state, do not return, while others do return.
तत्र केन मार्गेण गता नावर्तन्ते केन वा गताश्चावर्तन्त इत्यपेक्षायामाह -- यत्रेति।
When it is asked by which path those who go do not return and by which path those who go return, He says: ‘At which time.’
यत्र यस्मिन्काले प्रयाता योगिनोऽनावृत्तिं यान्ति यस्मिंश्च काले प्रयाता आवृत्तिं यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामीत्यन्वयः।
The construction is: I shall tell that time at which departing yogins go to non-return, and that time at which departing yogins go to return.
अत्र च रश्म्यनुसारी अतश्चायनेऽपि दक्षिण इति सूचितन्यायेनोत्तरायणादिकालविशेषस्मरणस्य विवक्षितत्वात्

Here, by the principle indicated in the statement ‘following the ray, and therefore even during the southern course,’ the mention of special times such as the northern course is intended in a particular sense.
कालशब्देन कालाभिमानिनीभिरातिवाहिकीभिर्देवताभिः प्राप्यो मार्ग उपलक्ष्यते
By the word ‘time’ is indicated the path reached through the conducting deities who preside over those times.
अतोऽयमर्थः -- यस्मिन्कालाभिमानिदेवतोपलक्षिते मार्गे प्रयाता योगिन उपासकाः कर्मिणश्च यथाक्रममनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं च यान्ति तं कालाभिमानिदेवतोपलक्षितं मार्गं कथयिष्यामीति।
Therefore the meaning is: I shall describe the path marked by deities presiding over time, by which departing yogins who are meditators and ritualists respectively attain non-return and return.
अग्निज्योतिषोः कालाभिमानित्वाभावेऽपि भूयसामहरादिशब्दोक्तानां कालाभिमानित्वात्तत्साहचर्यादाम्रवनमित्यादिवत्कालशब्देनोपलक्षणमविरुद्धम्।

Although fire and light are not deities presiding over time, most of those denoted by words such as ‘day’ are; through association with them, using ‘time’ as an inclusive designation is unobjectionable, as in expressions like ‘mango-grove.’
तत्रानावृत्तिमार्गमाह -- अग्निरिति।
There He states the path of non-return: ‘Fire.’
अग्निज्योतिःशब्दाभ्यां तेऽर्चिषमभिसंभवन्ति इति श्रुत्युक्तार्चिरभिमानिनी देवतोपलक्ष्यते।
By the words ‘fire’ and ‘light’ is indicated the deity presiding over flame mentioned in scripture: ‘They reach the flame.’
अहरिति दिवसाभिमानिनी। शुक्ल इति शुक्लपक्षाभिमानिनी। उत्तरायणरूपाः षण्मासा इत्युत्तरायणाभिमानिनी।
‘Day’ means the deity presiding over day; ‘bright’ the deity presiding over the bright fortnight; ‘the six months of the northern course’ the deity presiding over the northern course.
एतच्चान्यासामपि श्रुत्युक्तानां संवत्सरदेवलोकादिदेवतानामुपलक्षणार्थम्।
These also stand for the other deities mentioned in scripture, such as those of the year and the world of the gods.
एवंभूतो यो मार्गस्तत्र प्रयाता गता भगवदुपासका जनाः ब्रह्म प्राप्नुवन्ति। यतस्ते ब्रह्मविदः।
Those persons who worship the Lord and depart along such a path attain Brahman, because they are knowers of Brahman.
तथाच श्रुतिः तेऽर्चिषमभिसंभवन्ति ... मासेभ्यो देवलोकम् इति।

Thus scripture says: ‘They reach the flame; from the flame, day; from day, the waxing fortnight; from the waxing fortnight, the six months in which the sun goes north; from the months, the world of the gods.’
नहि सद्योमुक्तिभाजां सम्यग्दर्शननिष्ठानां गतिर्वा क्वचिदस्ति न तस्य प्राणा उत्क्रामन्ति इति श्रुतेः।
For those established in true knowledge who attain immediate liberation have no going anywhere at all, because scripture says: ‘His vital breaths do not depart.’
आवृत्तिमार्गमाह -- धूम इति।
He states the path of return: ‘Smoke.’
धूमाभिमानिनी देवता।
‘Smoke’ means the deity presiding over smoke.
रात्र्यादिशब्दैश्च पूर्ववदेव रात्रिकृष्णपक्षदक्षिणायनरूपषण्मासाभिमानिन्यस्तिस्रो देवता उपलक्ष्यन्ते।
As before, the words ‘night’ and the rest indicate the three deities presiding over night, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the southern course.
एताभिर्देवताभिरुपलक्षितो मार्गस्तत्र प्रयातः कर्मयोगी चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिस्तदुपलक्षितं स्वर्गलोकं प्राप्य
The karma-yogin who departs along the path marked by these deities reaches the lunar light, meaning the heavenly world indicated by it,
तत्रेष्टापूर्तकर्मफलं भुक्त्वा पुनरावर्तते।
and after enjoying there the fruit of sacrificial and charitable works, returns again.
अत्रापि श्रुतिः ते धूममभिसंभवन्ति ... ते चन्द्रं प्राप्यान्नं भवन्ति इत्यादिः।

Here too scripture says: ‘They reach smoke; from smoke, night; from night, the waning fortnight; from the waning fortnight, the six months in which the sun goes south; from the months, the world of the ancestors; from the world of the ancestors, the moon; having reached the moon they become food,’ and so on.
तदेवं निवृत्तिकर्मसहितोपासनया क्रममुक्तिः
Thus, through meditation accompanied by renunciatory action there is gradual liberation;
काम्यकर्मभिश्च स्वर्गभोगानन्तरमावृत्तिः
through desire-motivated actions, return after enjoyment in heaven;
निषिद्धकर्मभिस्तु नरकभोगानन्तरमावृत्तिः
through prohibited actions, return after suffering in hell;
क्षुद्रकर्मणां जन्तूनां त्वत्रैव पुनः पुनर्जन्मेति द्रष्टव्यम्।
and for creatures of petty actions, repeated birth here itself—this is to be understood.
उक्तौ मार्गावुपसंहरति -- शुक्लेति।
He sums up the two paths described: ‘Bright and dark.’
शुक्लाऽर्चिरादिगतिः प्रकाशमयत्वात् कृष्णा धूमादिगतिस्तमोमयत्वात्।
The path beginning with flame is ‘bright’ because it is luminous; the path beginning with smoke is ‘dark’ because it is made of darkness.
एते गती मार्गौ ज्ञानकर्माधिकारिणो जगतः शाश्वतेऽनादी संमते संसारस्यानादित्वात्।
These two courses, these paths for those qualified for knowledge and action, are regarded as eternal and beginningless for the world because saṃsāra itself is beginningless.
तयोरेकया शुक्लया निवृत्तिं मोक्षं याति।
By one of them, the bright path, one reaches cessation, liberation.
अन्यथा कृष्णया तु पुनरावर्तते।
By the other, the dark path, one returns again.
मार्गज्ञानफलं दर्शयन् भक्तियोगमुपसंहरति -- नैते इति।
Showing the fruit of knowing these paths, He concludes the yoga of devotion: ‘Knowing these.’
एते सृती मार्गौ हे पार्थ मोक्षसंसारप्रापकौ जानन्कश्चिदपि योगी न मुह्यति।
O Pārtha, any yogin who knows these two courses, the paths leading to liberation and saṃsāra, is not deluded.
सुखबुद्ध्या स्वर्गादिफलं न कामयते किंतु परमेश्वरनिष्ठ एव भवतीत्यर्थः।
He does not desire heaven and its results thinking them pleasurable, but remains established in the Supreme Lord alone; this is the meaning.
स्पष्टमन्यत्।
The rest is clear.
अध्यायार्थमष्टप्रश्नार्थनिर्णयं सफलमुपसंहरति -- वेदेष्विति।
He concludes, together with its fruit, the chapter’s subject: the determination of the meanings of the eight questions, saying: ‘In the Vedas.’
वेदेष्वध्ययनादिभिः यज्ञेष्वनुष्ठानादिभिः तपःसु कायशोषणादिभिः दानेषु सत्पात्रार्पणादिभिः यत्पुण्यफलमुपदिष्टं शास्त्रेषु तत्सर्वमत्येति

Whatever meritorious fruit is taught in scripture from study and the like of the Vedas, performance and the like of sacrifices, bodily austerity and the like, and gifts to worthy recipients and the like—he surpasses all of it.
ततोऽपि श्रेष्ठं योगैश्वर्यं प्राप्नोति।
He attains a yogic sovereignty superior even to that.
किं कृत्वा। इदमष्टप्रश्नार्थनिर्णयेनोक्तं तत्त्वं विदित्वा
By doing what? By knowing this truth stated through the determination of the meanings of the eight questions,
ततश्च योगी ज्ञानी भूत्वा परमुत्कृष्टमाद्यं जगन्मूलभूतस्थानं विष्णोः परमं पदं प्राप्नोति।
and then, becoming a yogin and knower, he attains the supreme, most excellent, primordial state that is the root of the universe—the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
